scope.applicability: the reviewed HighBar trace candidate and its helper health join

items.statement: At the reviewed HighBar candidate, serialization or allocation can throw before the trace exception boundary, constructor allocation can leak an opened descriptor, and a failed Record can be followed by a successful retry because failure is not permanently latched. Call sites ignore false and no production consumer authenticates failed state, so a valid-looking truncated prefix could qualify while trace I/O also changes command flow. The repair requires RAII ownership, a permanent nonthrowing failure latch visible to custody, second-call refusal, and unchanged command application.
items.title: Trace exceptions escaped and did not permanently expose failure

evidence.summary: B5 records the leader-exit descendant leak, bounded reproduction, and required group-custody cleanup semantics.

scope.applicability: the reviewed helper supervisor candidate and later native attempts

items.statement: The reviewed helper sends KILL only when waiting for the leader times out. If the leader exits after TERM while an owned descendant ignores TERM, cleanup reports unknown and leaves the descendant alive. An ordinary-process probe reproduced this and then reaped its own process. Cleanup must retain group custody after leader exit, escalate surviving owned members within the KILL budget, and verify settlement while preserving unknown for genuinely unresolved custody.
items.title: Leader exit did not trigger escalation for a surviving owned descendant
